newsitem.title: UK: NNPC says considering retroactive crude pricing.
newsitem.headline: NNPC says considering retroactive crude pricing.

text.p: Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) on Wednesday said it may price crude exports on a retroactive basis next year because of difficulties over recent months in setting contract terms.
NNPC also had decided to stick by the contract prices for December it announced last week despite complaints from a handful of trading companies, said NNPC head of marketing Taiwo Idemudia.
"We may set prices on the 10th of the month of lifting or retroactively," Idemudia said by telephone from Abuja.
"That is a recommendation I have made to the minister. I am contemplating doing that for the New Year but it will depend on the views of the minister."
Nigeria sells some 850,000 barrels a day (bpd) of crude through about 30 contracts with traders and refiners, adjusting prices every month according to spot market values.
Its biggest customers include European traders Glencore and Arcadia.
Idemudia said an ever-more opaque market in Nigerian crudes had made it very difficult to judge contract prices in the month ahead of lifting.

NNPC practice this year has been to announce prices in the middle of the month prior to the month of loading. A shift to retroactive pricing, after the month of loading, or pricing during the month of loading would mean most crude had traded before prices were announced.
"I'm sure most of our customers prefer early notice of pricing because it allows them to plan ahead," said Idemudia. "But they are making it impossible for us to do that."
Nigerian spot crude markets routinely go underground for at least the half of each month ahead of NNPC's pricing announcement.
Traders say most spot deals are kept strictly confidential. Off-market trades occasionally emerge in a bid to influence media price assessments.
Idemudia said December contract prices, announced last week, would remain unchanged despite a campaign by one or two large lifters to get the terms adjusted.
"There will be no price adjustment in December," he said. "We are not going to lower prices."
Spot Nigerian crude markets have come under pressure from an overhang of sweet grades in the Atlantic Basin leaving little room for profit for contract holders in December.
"Prices for December may not be the best but they are consistent with the pricing objective set out at the beginning of the year," said Idemudia.
NNPC aimed to allow its contract holders an 11 cent a barrel margin to cover business costs and profit, he said.
Using assessments from industry pricing service Platt's, Idemudia said margins over the past 12 months stood at 12.67 cents for Bonny Light/Qua Iboe and 13.29 cents for Forcados.
Actual margins, given routine downward manipulation of Platt's prices were likely to be much higher, traders said.
"When we come to the end of December we'll see that people have made a minimum of 11 cents a barrel," said Idemudia.
-- Richard Mably, London newsroom +44 171 542 8060
